title: Know where Flask's development server stops and deployment begins
masterChecklist: Framework survey and project labs: Flask/FastAPI/Django concepts; use one verified framework version per deep module
Web-framework concepts: routing, request/response, templates, middleware, background work
Deployment, containers, CI/CD concepts, release safety, monitoring, rollback
whyItMatters: A beginner can make a page appear with `flask run` and assume the service is ready for real users. That command starts a development server, not an operational production deployment.
simpleExplanation: Flask is the web application. A server accepts HTTP requests and calls that app through a WSGI interface. Flask's built-in `flask run` server and debugger are for local development only. A production setup uses an appropriate dedicated WSGI server or hosting platform, plus configuration, security, monitoring and rollback planning. A test client is different again: it exercises the app in process and does not listen on a port. This lesson teaches the boundary; it does not provision or expose a live server from the static LearnVerse site.
mentalModel: A classroom rehearsal, a closed-room inspection, and a public performance are three different situations. Test client, development server, and production serving each have their own purpose.
outcomes: Distinguish an in-process test client, local development server and production WSGI server.
Explain why debug mode must not be exposed to real users.
Keep a development-server call behind a main guard.
List concrete release checks before deploying a service.

realWorldExample.scenario: A team wants to publish the study-progress service after its local routes pass tests.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: Running the debugger on a reachable host can expose powerful developer tooling, while missing logs and rollback make failures hard to contain.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Keep tests in-process, use the development server only on a trusted local machine, then choose a supported WSGI deployment path and verify secrets, access control, health checks, logs, backup and rollback before users depend on it.

explanation: The route is application code; it is not itself an HTTP listening process.
The test client invokes the route in process and checks a response.
The main guard prevents `app.run()` from starting merely because a WSGI server imports the module.
Even with `debug=False`, Flask's built-in server remains a development server and is not a production deployment plan.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Explain why importing this module into a WSGI server must not also start its development server.

procedure: Run automated test-client checks before any network preview.
Use `flask --app service_entry run` only for trusted local development when Flask is installed.
Never use the interactive debugger on a reachable production deployment.
Choose and configure a dedicated WSGI server or managed platform for real use.
Document environment-specific configuration, secrets, health checks, logging, backups and rollback.
Perform a post-deploy smoke check and monitor errors before calling the release complete.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating `flask run --debug` as a quick production shortcut.
commonMistakes.why: The interactive debugger is powerful and the development server is not designed for production security or reliability.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use debug only in trusted local development and select a production serving path separately.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming a passing test client proves the app is reachable or healthy after deployment.
commonMistakes.why: In-process tests do not exercise DNS, reverse proxy, server process or real network configuration.
commonMistakes.avoid: Run a separate deployment smoke check and monitor the live service.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling `app.run()` unconditionally at module import time.
commonMistakes.why: A WSGI server importing the module could unexpectedly start another server.
commonMistakes.avoid: Place local development start code under `if __name__ == '__main__'`.

lab.title: Separate app tests, local preview and production release
lab.safety: The browser tests a launch guard only. It does not start Flask or a server; Flask's development server is not suitable for production.
guidedSteps: Allow preview only when --local-preview is explicitly present.
Return a Boolean; do not start a server.
Compare with the guarded real Flask app.run example.
checks: The browser never starts Flask's development server.
hints: Do not call app.run in this exercise.
lab.solutionExplanation: The explicit flag reduces accidental local launch. Production deployment requires a suitable WSGI server or hosting platform, not the development server.
challenges: Predict what happens to app.run when this file is imported by another module.
Find the bug: start app.run(debug=True) at module import time on a public host.
Classify each action as test, local development or production: test_client, flask run, dedicated WSGI serving.

choices: A passing test-client request proves the deployed service is reachable
The test client checks app behavior in process; deployment needs separate serving and smoke checks
simulation.explanation: The test client does not exercise a live server or network path.

lab.testCode:
assert local_preview_allowed(['app.py','--local-preview']) is True
assert local_preview_allowed(['app.py']) is False
print('PASS: explicit local preview gate')

projectConnection.milestone: Add a health route and separate in-process testing from a documented production release checklist.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: The local health test is specified, the development server remains local-only, and deployment is not claimed until a dedicated serving path and smoke check are actually verified.

assessment.question: Does `app.test_client()` publish the service?
assessment.explanation: It invokes the app in process without a public listening server.

assessment.question: Is Flask's built-in server production-ready merely because debug is false?
Why put app.run under a main guard?
assessment.answer: To prevent a server from starting when the module is imported.
assessment.explanation: Production WSGI servers import or obtain the app callable separately.
